references.text: The preceding context describes the daily burnt offering with two lambs, one in the morning and one in the evening, which this verse completes the instructions for.
Parallel text describing the daily burnt offering with two lambs, a grain offering, and a drink offering, morning and evening, as a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
Elijah offered on Carmel 'at the time of the evening sacrifice' (בַּעֲלוֹת הַמִּנְחָה), referring to the fixed time for the evening offering described in Exodus 29:41.
Ezra prayed at the time of the evening sacrifice (מִנְחַת הָעֶרֶב), referring to the daily sacrificial practice established in Exodus 29:41.
The angel Gabriel came to Daniel 'at the time of the evening sacrifice' (כְּעֵת מִנְחַת־עָרֶב), referring to the established time of offering.
Noah offered burnt offerings, and the Lord smelled a pleasing aroma (רֵיחַ הַנִּיחֹחַ), the same expression used in Exodus 29:41.
The burnt offering is described as a fire offering with a pleasing aroma to the Lord (אִשֵּׁה רֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ לַיהוָה), the same terminology found in Exodus 29:41.
The grain offering (מִנְחָה) is described here in detail, the same grain offering that must accompany the evening lamb in Exodus 29:41.
Christ's sacrifice is described as a pleasing aroma to God (ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας), fulfilling the symbolism of Old Testament sacrifices from Exodus 29:41.
Paul describes the Philippians' gift as a pleasing aroma (ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας), an offering that God accepts with joy, using language drawn from sacrificial texts such as Exodus 29:41.
Identical legal command regarding the twilight sacrifice in two different law collections confirming ritual continuity.
The general division of the day's two lambs (morning/evening) provides context for the details of the twilight sacrifice.
Distinguishes between the fixed daily offering (Exodus) and additional festival offerings that come on top of this.
Confirms that the daily offering is the fixed foundation upon which other festival offerings are built.
Prophetic restoration of the same principle of the daily offering in the coming age.
Specifies the technical quantity of flour and oil for the daily lamb mentioned in the source verse.
